cards.front: Recall a key point about Rhythm Metre and Tempo
cards.back: Simple time divides beats into 2 (2/4, 3/4, 4/4); compound time divides into 3 (6/8, 9/8, 12/8) — the feel is fundamentally different.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rhythm Metre and Tempo
cards.back: Syncopation places emphasis on off-beats or weak beats — it creates rhythmic tension and is central to jazz, blues and popular music.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rhythm Metre and Tempo
cards.back: Polyrhythm is two or more conflicting rhythmic patterns played simultaneously — common in African and Caribbean music traditions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rhythm Metre and Tempo
cards.back: Hemiola creates a temporary shift of metre (e.g. feeling 2 groups of 3 as 3 groups of 2) — used from Renaissance to pop music.

cards.front: What should you know about music exam tips?
cards.back: Identify the METRE (simple/compound), TEMPO (Italian terms), and rhythmic DEVICES (syncopation, hemiola, polyrhythm). Explain the EFFECT of each rhythmic feature.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Rhythm is just the beat of the music. Correct: Rhythm encompasses metre (how beats are grouped), tempo (speed), and rhythmic PATTERNS (syncopation, polyrhythm, hemiola, dotted rhythms). The exam requires you to identify specific rhythmic features using correct terminology — not just say it has a beat.
Identify three different rhythmic features in a piece of music. Use precise terminology and explain the effect of each feature on the character of the music.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: Rhythm Metre and Tempo
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Show knowledge of Rhythm Metre and Tempo using appropriate musical vocabulary (e.g. terminology for elements, devices, and contexts).

Rhythm Metre and Tempo is a key element of GCSE Music requiring theoretical understanding and practical application. The AQA specification requires you to identify, describe and analyse this element in set works and unfamiliar music. cards.front: Applying Rhythm Metre and Tempo in Performance and Composition
cards.back: Understanding rhythm metre and tempo informs your performing (AO1) and composing (AO2) work. In performance, awareness of rhythm metre and tempo helps you make interpretive decisions that serve the music. In composition, rhythm metre and tempo provides the building blocks of your creative work — the choices you make about this element shape the identity and coherence of your piece.

cards.front: Exam Technique for Rhythm Metre and Tempo Questions
cards.back: In the AQA GCSE Music listening exam, questions about rhythm metre and tempo typically ask you to: identify features by ear; describe how they are used; explain their effect; compare features between extracts. The key to success is precise terminology — never use vague language.
